gospels/mark.file: Shorter ending of Mark 16 from Codex Sinaiticus.png
gospels/mark.alt: Codex Sinaiticus, fourth century: the Gospel of Mark ending at 16:8, with the shorter ending that a later hand supplied
gospels/mark.caption: Codex Sinaiticus, fourth century: Mark ends at 16:8, and the verses printed after it in later Bibles are absent. British Library.

gospels/matthew.alt: Codex Sinaiticus, fourth century: the first page of the Gospel of Matthew, the genealogy and the birth
gospels/matthew.caption: Codex Sinaiticus, fourth century: the first page of Matthew, 1:1 to 2:5.

gospels/luke.file: Dublin, Chester Beatty Ms Papyrus 45 BP I ff.13-14 Luke 11.50-12.12; 12.18-37; 12.42-13.1; 13.jpg
gospels/luke.alt: Papyrus 45, Chester Beatty Library, Dublin, about 200 to 250 CE: two leaves of the Gospel of Luke
gospels/luke.caption: Papyrus 45 (Chester Beatty I), about 200 to 250 CE: Luke 11 to 13, among the oldest copies of any gospel. Chester Beatty Library, Dublin.

gospels/thomas.file: Gospel of Thomas - Nag Hammadi II-35.jpg
gospels/thomas.alt: Nag Hammadi Codex II, page 35, the Gospel of Thomas in Coptic, fourth century
gospels/thomas.caption: Nag Hammadi Codex II, page 35: the Gospel of Thomas in Coptic, the only complete copy, found in Egypt in 1945.

gospels/thomas/sayings.file: Gospel of Thomas - Nag Hammadi II-36.jpg
gospels/thomas/sayings.alt: Nag Hammadi Codex II, page 36, the Gospel of Thomas in Coptic
gospels/thomas/sayings.caption: Nag Hammadi Codex II, page 36 of the Gospel of Thomas, the Coptic text behind this translation.

gospels/thomas/sayings-patterson-meyer.file: Gospel of Thomas - Nag Hammadi II-39.jpg
gospels/thomas/sayings-patterson-meyer.alt: Nag Hammadi Codex II, page 39, the Gospel of Thomas in Coptic
gospels/thomas/sayings-patterson-meyer.caption: Nag Hammadi Codex II, page 39 of the Gospel of Thomas.

gospels/thomas/set-aside.file: Gospel of Thomas - Nag Hammadi II-51.jpg
gospels/thomas/set-aside.alt: Nag Hammadi Codex II, page 51, the last page of the Gospel of Thomas with its title
gospels/thomas/set-aside.caption: Nag Hammadi Codex II, page 51: the end of the Gospel of Thomas and its title, written at the close as ancient scribes did.

gospels/thomas/correlation.file: Preface and Sayings of Jesus - Gospel of Thomas (3rd C), verso - BL Papyrus 1531.jpg
gospels/thomas/correlation.alt: Papyrus Oxyrhynchus 654, third century: the prologue and first sayings of the Gospel of Thomas in Greek, British Library Papyrus 1531
gospels/thomas/correlation.caption: Papyrus Oxyrhynchus 654, third century: the prologue and sayings 1 to 7 of Thomas in Greek, older than the Coptic copy. British Library, Papyrus 1531.

gospels/synoptic-problem.alt: Papyrus 45, about 200 to 250 CE: a fragment of Mark 8:35 to 9:1
gospels/synoptic-problem.caption: Papyrus 45, about 200 to 250 CE: Mark 8:35 to 9:1. Mark is the source that Matthew and Luke rewrote.

gospels/discrepancies.alt: Codex Vaticanus, fourth century: the end of the Gospel of Luke and the beginning of John
gospels/discrepancies.caption: Codex Vaticanus, fourth century: the end of Luke and the opening of John on one page. Vatican Library.

gospels/discrepancies/genealogies.alt: Book of Kells, folio 29r: Liber generationis, the opening of Matthew's genealogy of Jesus
gospels/discrepancies/genealogies.caption: Book of Kells, about 800 CE, folio 29r: Liber generationis, the first words of Matthew's genealogy. Trinity College Dublin.

gospels/discrepancies/last-supper.file: The Last Supper - Leonardo Da Vinci - High Resolution 32x16.jpg
gospels/discrepancies/last-supper.alt: Leonardo da Vinci, The Last Supper, 1495 to 1498, Santa Maria delle Grazie, Milan
gospels/discrepancies/last-supper.caption: Leonardo da Vinci, The Last Supper (1495 to 1498), Santa Maria delle Grazie, Milan: the meal John places before the Passover and the synoptics at it.

paul/seven-letters.file: Ann Arbor, University of Michigan P.Mich.inv. 6238 (Papyrus 46) fol. 158r Eph 6, 20–Gal 1, 8.jpg
paul/seven-letters.alt: Papyrus 46, about 200 CE: the end of Ephesians and the beginning of Galatians, University of Michigan
paul/seven-letters.caption: Papyrus 46, about 200 CE, the oldest collection of Paul of Tarsus's letters: the end of Ephesians and the opening of Galatians. University of Michigan.

paul/acts-galatians.file: Conversion on the Way to Damascus-Caravaggio (c.1600-1).jpg
paul/acts-galatians.alt: Caravaggio, Conversion on the Way to Damascus, about 1601, Santa Maria del Popolo, Rome
paul/acts-galatians.caption: Caravaggio, Conversion on the Way to Damascus (about 1601), Santa Maria del Popolo, Rome: the scene Acts tells three times and Galatians once, differently.

paul/paul-against-jesus.alt: Papyrus 46: the first page of the Epistle to the Galatians in Greek
paul/paul-against-jesus.caption: Papyrus 46, about 200 CE: the opening of Galatians, the letter in which Paul of Tarsus sets his gospel against the men who knew Jesus.

paul/james.alt: Icon of James the Just, brother of Jesus and leader of the Jerusalem church
paul/james.caption: James the Just, the brother of Jesus who led the Jerusalem church, in a traditional icon.

the-islamic-dilemma.alt: A Qur'an manuscript in Maghribi script showing Sūrat al-Māʾida, the fifth sūra
the-islamic-dilemma.caption: Sūrat al-Māʾida in a Qur'an written in Maghribi script. Verses 46 to 48 of this sūra, the Injīl given to ʿĪsā and the Qur'an as guardian over the earlier scripture, are the ground on which the dilemma is answered.

quran/table.alt: Juan de Juanes, The Last Supper, about 1562, Museo del Prado
quran/table.caption: Juan de Juanes, The Last Supper (about 1562), Museo del Prado, Madrid. The Qur'an's table from heaven (5:112 to 115) is the sign the disciples asked for.

resources/sources.alt: Codex Vaticanus, fourth century: the end of 2 Thessalonians and the beginning of Hebrews
resources/sources.caption: Codex Vaticanus, fourth century, one of the two oldest complete Greek Bibles: the end of 2 Thessalonians and the opening of Hebrews. Vatican Library.

resources/objections.alt: Codex Sinaiticus, fourth century: a page of Matthew 6 with the Lord's Prayer
resources/objections.caption: Codex Sinaiticus, fourth century: Matthew 6:4 to 32, with the Lord's Prayer. British Library.
